anchors.paper_title: Frontotemporal bursting supports human working memory
anchors.reason: Dataset README names this paper as its associated publication; the authors match, and it reports the iEEG recordings from MFG/MTG during a visual working memory task (the same data).

metadata.methods_description: Intracranial EEG was recorded from epilepsy patients during an object working memory task with 1000 ms fixation, 1500 ms encoding, and 3998 ms delay. Data were preprocessed with artifact rejection, and trials per channel were concatenated and zero-padded into EDF format.

citation_details.title: The role of the right temporal lobe in neural network mechanisms during working memory encoding
citation_details.author: Peiran Yu, Liping Pan, Jiajing Wang, Wenjuan Wu, Yuncong Cao, Fangfang Hao, Yunfan Wang, Yujing Zhu, Yijun Song
citation_details.abstract: Background Visual working memory (vWM) impairment is common in patients with temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE) and is more severe in those with right TLE (RTLE), suggesting the significant role of right temporal lobe in WM processes. Methods We recruited patients with left TLE (LTLE group, n = 20), RTLE (RTLE group, n = 20) and 35 healthy controls (Control), and examined their vWM performance while simultaneously recording task-based EEG. The alterations in the neural oscillations and neural network were analyzed during the WM encoding phase. In addition, we examined the relationship between the neural oscillations and WM performance, as well as the relationship between the neural network and WM performance, to further explore the role of the right temporal lobe in WM encoding. Results Remarkably lower accuracy (both p < 0.001) and significantly longer response times (LTLE vs. Control: p = 0.026; RTLE vs. Control: p < 0.001) were found in both LTLE and RTLE groups compared with controls. citation_details.title: Processing of different word list lengths during encoding and retrieval in Broca’s area
citation_details.author: Viktors Veliks, Aleksandrs Koļesovs, Juris Porozovs, Dmitrijs Igonins
citation_details.abstract: Broca's area is a region of the brain involved in the processing of verbal information, including memory encoding and retrieval. This study examined differences in the neural correlates of encoding and retrieval in Broca's area using word lists of varying lengths. Differences in the encoding and retrieval processes were assessed using word lists of different lengths: short (2-29), medium (30-59), and long (60-225) Latvian language nouns. In total, 23 participants completed the memory task. Each participant performed memory tasks with two short lists, two medium lists, and one long list, with varying list lengths within each diapason. We considered the activity of the F3 and F7 to represent our region of interest. We compared time-frequency (TF) data from encoding and retrieval across list lengths.
